content:
# Baruch Chapter 2 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Baruch 2 (35 verses)
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 17

---

## Disagreement 001 — v.2: "great evils" vs. "great disasters"

**EMET:** "great evils which have not been done"
**LOGOS:** "great disasters such as have never before been done"
**PNEUMA:** "disasters greater than anything that has happened"
**Issue:** Greek kaka megala = great evils. "Disasters" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) is more idiomatic in modern English; "evils" (EMET) is more literal but may imply moral evil rather than catastrophe. Consensus: "great disasters."

---

## Disagreement 002 — v.3: Structural — embedded quotation or summary

**EMET:** Presents v.3 as direct continuation of v.2
**LOGOS:** Same
**PNEUMA:** Sets it off as "including the most terrible thing of all"
**Issue:** PNEUMA adds an emotional framing phrase not in the Greek. Consensus follows the Greek structure without addition.

---

## Disagreement 003 — v.4: "to be subject" vs. "given over to subjection"

**EMET:** "to be subject to all the kingdoms"
**LOGOS:** "given over to subjection under all the kingdoms"
**PNEUMA:** "handed us over to all the surrounding kingdoms"
**Issue:** Greek hypotassesthai = to be put under/subjected. All acceptable. LOGOS preserves the "given over" (paredōken) verb more explicitly. Consensus: "gave them over to subjection under."

---

## Disagreement 004 — v.6: "shame of face" vs. "open shame"

**EMET:** "shame of face"
**LOGOS:** "open shame"
**PNEUMA:** "covered in shame"
**Issue:** Same issue as ch.1 v.15. Greek aischynē prosōpou = shame of the face. This is the second occurrence of the confessional formula; should be rendered consistently. Consensus: "open shame" (consistent with ch.1 ruling).

---

## Disagreement 005 — v.8: "entreat the favor" vs. "seek the face" vs. "seek the Lord's face"

**EMET:** "did not entreat the favor of the Lord"
**LOGOS:** "did not entreat the face of the Lord"
**PNEUMA:** "did not seek the Lord's face"
**Issue:** Greek deēthēnai tou prosōpou kyriou = to beseech the face of the Lord. The Semitism "seek/entreat the face" is standard biblical idiom. Consensus: "seek the face of the Lord" — preserves idiom with natural English verb.

---

## Disagreement 006 — v.9: "kept watch over" vs. "watched"

**EMET:** "the Lord kept watch over the evils"
**LOGOS:** "the Lord kept watch over the disasters"
**PNEUMA:** "The Lord watched as the disasters unfolded"
**Issue:** Greek egrēgorēsen = he was watchful/kept vigil. The image of God as vigilant watchman over judgment is striking. PNEUMA adds "unfolded" as interpretive expansion. Consensus: "kept watch over."

---

## Disagreement 007 — v.11: Doxology formula — "mighty hand"

**EMET:** "with a mighty hand and signs and wonders and with great power and with an outstretched arm"
**LOGOS:** "with a mighty hand, and with signs and wonders and great power and an outstretched arm"
**PNEUMA:** "with a mighty hand, with signs and wonders, with great power and an outstretched arm"
**Issue:** Punctuation and conjunction placement only. All agents agree on the content. Consensus: follows LOGOS/PNEUMA without double "with."

---

## Disagreement 008 — v.12: "acted impiously" vs. "been ungodly" vs. "been wicked"

**EMET:** "acted impiously"
**LOGOS:** "been ungodly"
**PNEUMA:** "been wicked"
**Issue:** Greek ēsebēsamen = we acted impiously/ungodly. "Ungodly" (LOGOS) is the standard English cognate. EMET preserves the active voice. Consensus: "been ungodly."

---

## Disagreement 009 — v.13: "few" vs. "remnant"

**EMET:** "left as a few"
**LOGOS:** "left as a remnant"
**PNEUMA:** "only a remnant"
**Issue:** Greek eis oligostous = to the point of very few. "Remnant" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) is theologically loaded in a positive direction (the faithful remnant); the Greek is simply "very few," which can be purely numerical. Consensus: "left as a remnant" — the theological connotation fits the context.

---

## Disagreement 010 — v.17: "glory and justification" vs. "glory and righteousness"

**EMET:** "glory and justification"
**LOGOS:** "glory and justification"
**PNEUMA:** "praise you or declare that you are righteous"
**Issue:** Greek doxan kai dikaiosynēn = glory and righteousness/justification. EMET and LOGOS preserve both nouns; PNEUMA renders as verbs. The parallelism of two nouns given to the Lord is structurally important. Consensus: "glory and justification" — the unusual noun "justification" is retained as it captures the forensic nuance.

---

## Disagreement 011 — v.18: Subject of giving glory

**EMET:** "the soul that is grieved... these give glory"
**LOGOS:** "the person who is deeply grieved... it is that person who gives"
**PNEUMA:** "that person will give you glory"
**Issue:** EMET retains "soul" (psychē) as subject; LOGOS and PNEUMA shift to "person." The soul-language is significant in Baruch's anthropology. Consensus: "the soul that is deeply grieved."

---

## Disagreement 012 — v.19: "lay before you our supplication" vs. "bring our supplication before you"

**EMET:** "lay before you our supplication"
**LOGOS:** "bring our supplication before you"
**PNEUMA:** "coming to you"
**Issue:** Greek prospherontes = bringing/presenting. A liturgical term for offering. EMET's "lay before" captures the presentational nuance. Consensus: "bring our supplication before you."

---

## Disagreement 013 — v.23: "voice of rejoicing" refrain

**EMET:** "voice of rejoicing and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride"
**LOGOS:** Same
**PNEUMA:** "no more voices of bride and bridegroom, no more celebrations" — reorders and condenses
**Issue:** The four-fold "voice of X" pattern is a direct Jeremiah allusion (Jer 7:34, 16:9, 25:10, 33:11). PNEUMA's reordering loses the Jeremianic pattern. Consensus: retains all four pairs in order.

---

## Disagreement 014 — v.24: "bones brought out" — active or passive

**EMET:** "the bones of our kings... would be brought out"
**LOGOS:** "would be brought out from their resting places"
**PNEUMA:** "dragged out of their graves"
**Issue:** LOGOS adds "resting places" (gentler); PNEUMA "dragged" (more brutal). Greek exerchesthai = to come out/be brought out. Neutral Greek; consensus stays neutral.

---

## Disagreement 015 — v.25: "heat of day" and "frost of night"

**EMET:** "heat of day and the frost of night"
**LOGOS:** "scorching heat of the day and the cold of the night"
**PNEUMA:** "blazing sun by day and the bitter cold at night"
**Issue:** Greek kauma = heat/burning; pagetos = frost/cold. LOGOS and PNEUMA add intensifiers. "Scorching" and "bitter" are interpretive. Consensus: "heat of day and the frost of night" — retains simplicity.

---

## Disagreement 016 — v.30: "change of heart" vs. "turn to their heart"

**EMET:** "they will turn to their heart"
**LOGOS:** "they will have a change of heart"
**PNEUMA:** "they will finally come to their senses"
**Issue:** Greek epistrepsousin epi tēn kardian = they will return/turn toward the heart. This is a Hebrew idiom for reflection and repentance. LOGOS "change of heart" is natural English. PNEUMA "come to their senses" loses the heart-theology. Consensus: "they will take it to heart" or "will have a change of heart."

---

## Disagreement 017 — v.35: "no longer remove" vs. "never again uproot"

**EMET:** "no more remove my people Israel"
**LOGOS:** "no longer remove my people Israel"
**PNEUMA:** "never again uproot my people Israel"
**Issue:** Greek ou prosthēsō eti = I will no longer add/continue. The verb is not specifically "uproot." PNEUMA's "uproot" adds an agricultural metaphor. Consensus: "no longer remove."
